interactions.summary: Jiang stops the Adam-versus-Eve blame debate and asks instead why Dante so strongly elevates women in heaven, prompting answers that maternal love models selflessness and that Beatrice is the initiating source of Dante's love.
Students then test a social-reading hypothesis: women are denied teaching authority in ordinary society, so Dante may invert that order in heaven partly as a response to how the Church treats women.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student answers with Jiang brief confirmation

claims.claim: Jiang reframes the issue away from whether Adam or Eve is to blame and toward why Dante gives women extraordinary authority in heaven, with Beatrice teaching Dante and Mary elevated above Jesus.
A student proposes that Dante treats maternal love as the earthly form closest to selflessness, and Jiang explicitly agrees that Dante thinks very highly of mothers.
claims.temporal_scope: Student interpretation with Jiang confirmation voiced on 2026-06-18.

claims.claim: Another student argues that feminine love is central because Dante's movement toward love begins through Beatrice.
Students probe whether Dante's heavenly elevation of women works as an inversion of a society where women were not permitted to teach or enjoy equal standing, and Jiang accepts this line of thought.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang escalates the gender reversal by insisting the real question is why Dante lets women teach heaven's truths and places Mary above Jesus.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Mary is elevated more than Jesus
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This keeps the lecture's provocation sharp and sets up the social critique that follows.

signature_moments.moment: Maternal love is floated as the nearest earthly image of selfless love, and Jiang ratifies that Dante treats mothers with unusual reverence.
signature_moments.source_phrase: maternal love is the closest thing to selflessness
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the packet a concrete moral mechanism rather than leaving female elevation as a vague symbolic flourish.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Presented as Dante's closest earthly analogy for selfless love.
A student's term for the Beatrice-centered source of Dante's awakening into love.

uncertainty_notes.note: Most concrete motives in this packet are student hypotheses that Jiang partially validates rather than fully developed Jiang arguments.
